start.text: Abuja. Federal Capital Territory. Wide roads, big gates, bigger dreams. You are nine years old.

home_lapo.speaker: Mama
home_lapo.text: One room in Nyanya. Mama sells pepper and tomatoes by the junction. Last night, garri without sugar again. This morning she says: "{name}, after school, come help me for the stall o."

choices.text: Help Mama at the stall every day
choices.result: You learn to count change faster than your teacher. Your homework suffers small.

choices.text: Beg to focus on your books
choices.result: Mama sighs, but she lets you read under the one bulb. When NEPA allows.

fees.speaker: Headmaster
fees.text: Assembly. The headmaster reads names. Yours is on the list. "Those owing school fees, go home and come back with your parents." The whole school turns to look.

choices.text: Sell sachet water at the junction with Tunde

effects.log: Sold pure water at nine to help pay school fees.

choices.result: Tunde shows you the best spot: under the bridge, where the danfo drivers stop. By Friday, half the fees are paid.
Uncle Sylvester gives a long speech about 'hard work' and ₦500. He will remind the family of this ₦500 for the next twenty years.

choices.text: Stay home and study from a borrowed textbook
choices.result: You miss two weeks of school, but you finish the borrowed textbook. Twice.

home_average.speaker: Daddy
home_average.text: A two-bedroom flat in Gwarinpa. Daddy is a civil servant at the Federal Secretariat; Mummy trades fabrics in Wuse Market. Not rich, not suffering. Daddy says: "{name}, this term, I want to see results."

choices.result: The lesson teacher smells of Robb and wisdom. Your maths improves.

choices.text: Help Mummy at her fabric stall on Saturdays
choices.result: You learn that every customer says "last price" and nobody means it.
You are not Okocha, but the whole estate knows your name.

friends.text: Break time. Tunde, the boy who always comes early because his mama opens shop at 6, sits alone with nothing to eat. Slim, the boy with new shoes every term, waves you over: "My guy, copy my homework. I get the answers."

effects.log: Shared lunch with Tunde. He never forgot.

choices.result: Tunde splits your bread exactly in half. "I go pay you back one day," he says. He means it.
Full marks, zero learning. Slim winks: "Stick with me."
Tunde brings the jokes, Slim brings the gist. You bring yourself.

end.text: Primary school ends. Your mother cries at the graduation. Your father pretends he is not crying. Somewhere in Maitama, a boy your age has just been given his first car keys. For when he turns sixteen.

start.text: Secondary school. New uniform (yours is your cousin's old one, if you are a Lapo Baby; new from the tailor if not). Same Tunde. Same Slim. New problems.

lapo_school.text: Community secondary school, Nyanya. Forty-eight students per class, one fan, no NEPA. The chemistry lab is a picture of a chemistry lab. But the teachers who care, really care.

choices.result: Your argument that 'NEPA should be renamed Never Expect Power Always' wins the inter-school round.

choices.text: Run errands for traders after school
choices.result: Small money, steady money. Your schoolbag smells like crayfish.

average_school.text: Federal Government College. Boarding school. Senior students who think they are the Army. The food is a crime scene, but the teachers are decent and the alumni network is long.

choices.result: You build a robot from a biscuit tin. It moves forward, once.

choices.text: Become the class 'provost' who sells provisions
choices.result: Indomie at ₦50 profit per pack. You are the Dangote of Hostel B.

big_event.speaker: Bolaji
big_event.text: Inter-school quiz at a 'big' school in Maitama. A convoy rolls in: two Prados, one siren. Out steps Bolaji Danjuma-Adeyemi, son of (fictional) Senator Danjuma-Adeyemi. He scans your team. "You guys came by bus? Respect, honestly."

effects.log: Met Bolaji, a Nepo Baby, at a quiz in Maitama.

choices.result: He gives you his number. And his driver's number, 'in case'.

choices.text: Beat his team in the quiz

effects.log: Beat the Maitama school in a quiz. Bolaji clapped.

choices.result: You win. Bolaji claps, genuinely. His father's aide does not.
Pride is free. For now.

peer.speaker: Slim
peer.text: Slim finds you after school. New iPhone, school shirt untucked. "My guy, there's this runs. You just go collect package for one oga for Lugbe, bring am come. ₦10k per trip. No questions."

effects.log: Did 'no questions' runs for Slim at fifteen.

choices.result: Two trips, ₦20k. The second package was heavier. You did not ask.
Tunde says, "Guy, that one na trouble." Slim calls you 'Pastor' for a month.

socials.text: Everyone is on Tiklok now. Your classmate's skit about Nigerian mothers and slippers has 300k views. You open the app.

choices.result: Your third video ("POV: NEPA takes light during WAEC revision") gets 40k views. You understand the algorithm a little.
Four hours vanish. You learn nothing. It was lovely.

crush.text: There is someone in SS2 who laughs at your jokes. Innocent butterflies. You consider writing a note.

choices.result: They reply: "You're funny." You re-read it 400 times.
Love can wait. WAEC cannot.

waec.text: WAEC season. 'Expo' is selling on WhatsApp: ₦5,000 for 'verified' answers. Half the class has bought it.

then.toast: WAEC: 5 credits including Maths and English!

else.toast: WAEC: Maths missed by one mark.

choices.result: You read by candlelight. Results come out.

else.toast: The expo was for last year's paper. Of course.

choices.result: You pay. You pray.

dropout.text: End of secondary school. Money is tight; university will cost. Some people your age are already making money in the market, on the road, online.

choices.text: Resit WAEC next year, then JAMB
choices.result: One more year, one more try. This time, you pass.

choices.text: Drop out and start hustling now

effects.log: Dropped out after secondary school to hustle.

jamb.text: JAMB day. The CBT centre in Garki has three working computers and four hundred candidates.

else.toast: Missed the cut-off. Tried again next year and got in.

choices.result: Results drop at midnight. Your phone shakes in your hand.

start.text: University of Abuja, Gwagwalada campus. Hostel with eight people in a four-person room. Somebody's mattress is older than you. Freedom smells like burnt noodles.

choices.result: They meet in a classroom with one socket and seventeen extension boxes.

choices.text: Start a hostel hustle selling snacks
choices.result: Gala and Fanta at 2 a.m. You are a public service.
Your CGPA thanks you. Your social life does not.

strike.text: ASUU is on strike. Again. Indefinitely. "Go home, students." Your four-year course is now a five-year course, minimum.

choices.text: Learn to code from free videos
choices.result: Data costs more than food, but by month six you build your first website.

choices.text: Run a POS stand in Gwagwalada
choices.result: Withdrawal charges are a goldmine. You learn the true face of Nigerian banking.

choices.text: Follow Slim to the 'lab' in Lugbe

effects.log: Learned 'the format' in Slim's yahoo lab during an ASUU strike.

choices.result: Ring lights, three laptops, and 'the format'. You make ₦60k in a week. Your stomach turns a little.

cult.text: Strike over. On campus, two groups are recruiting. One wears berets and uses words like 'protection'. The other is the Rotaract club, which mostly does fundraisers.

then.toast: A rival group attacks. You spend two weeks in the clinic.

then.log: Joined a campus cult. Got hurt for it.

choices.result: Initiation is not a party. It is a lesson in how fast bad decisions get serious.
You organise a charity football match. Even the VC shows up.

mentor.speaker: Mrs. Okafor
mentor.text: Mrs. Okafor, your economics lecturer, stops you after class. "You ask good questions. My consultancy needs an intern this holiday. Unpaid. You will work hard. You will learn plenty."

effects.log: Interned with Mrs. Okafor. She became a mentor.

choices.result: You make 300 photocopies and two good impressions. She starts introducing you as 'my person'.
Money now. Maybe doors later. Maybe.

guru.speaker: Prophet Profit
guru.text: Your timeline is full of Prophet Profit, standing beside a Lamborghini (rented). "Forex mentorship: ₦50,000. 95% win rate. Students only discount!"

effects.log: Paid a forex guru ₦50k for a course.

choices.result: The 'course' is four YouTube links and a Telegram group where he sells a second course.

choices.text: Learn trading from free books instead
choices.result: Boring, slow, and actually useful.

nepo_party.speaker: Bolaji
nepo_party.text: Bolaji, now in a private university that charges in dollars, is throwing a party in Maitama. He invites you, if you know him. If you do not, the caterer is hiring waiters for ₦15k a night.

choices.result: You spend ₦20k on an outfit to look like you belong. A senator's aide asks what your father does. You meet three people who will matter.

choices.text: Work the party as a waiter
choices.result: You serve jollof to people your age who don't say thank you. One of them tips ₦20k without looking at you.

love.speaker: {love}
love.text: At a friend's birthday, you meet {love}. Sharp, funny, studying law, and completely unimpressed by fake people. (Both of you are over 18.)

choices.result: You walk them to the gate at 2 a.m. and forget your own name on the way back.

final.text: Final year. Project, defence, and one lecturer who 'cannot find' your file. Some classmates are dropping out to chase money.

effects.log: Graduated from the University of Abuja.

choices.result: Second Class Upper. Your mother tells the whole street.

start.text: Your call-up letter drops. One year of national service. Without the NYSC certificate, most government and big corporate jobs will lock you out. With it, you will spend a year being called 'Corper'.

choices.result: Freedom now. Paperwork problems later.

camp.text: Orientation camp, Kubwa. Three weeks of drills at 4:30 a.m., white shorts, and Mammy market suya at midnight. The soldiers shout. The cooks do not care.

choices.result: You become platoon leader. Everyone knows you by the end of week one.

choices.text: Save energy, avoid drills where possible
choices.result: You perfect the art of hiding behind the clinic.

mammy.text: Mammy market at night: fried yam, phone charging for ₦200, and every corps member in Nigeria sharing gist. Someone you met in camp asks you to join their table.

choices.result: New contacts from five states. One of them is starting a logistics business.
One generator, twelve extensions, a business plan.

posting_talk.text: Posting day is close. Rumour says Nepo Baby corpers are already 'confirmed' for Abuja and Lagos. Around camp, fixers whisper that they can keep you in Abuja. For a price.

fixers.text: Behind the camp clinic, the fixers gather. Each one has a reputation, if you know who to ask. Stars shown above their heads come from other corpers' reviews.

choices.text: Walk away and let fate decide

abuja_posting.text: Your letter says FCT, Abuja. You exhale. Nearby, a Nepo Baby corper did not even come to camp, and he is also posted to Abuja. Of course.

choices.text: Take a PPA at a federal ministry
choices.result: Your job is to carry files from Room 12 to Room 14. Twice a day.

choices.text: Take a PPA at a tech startup in Wuse
choices.result: The startup has a PlayStation and no salaries. You learn plenty.

choices.text: Report to your PPA and make the most of it
choices.result: Eleven months. Allawee every month: ₦77,000, when it comes. You learn a new place, new food, new people.

pass_out.text: Passing out parade. Khaki ironed sharp, certificate in hand. Real life starts now. Abuja is waiting, with its rent, its traffic, and its opportunities.

start.text: You are an adult in Abuja now. Rent is due weekly in this game (be grateful: real landlords want two years upfront). Your goal: financial freedom. Talent matters. Grind matters. Money and connections matter more.

dropout_intro.text: No certificate, no waiting. Some doors are closed to you: banks, ministries, big corporates. Others are wide open: business, trading, content, the road. And Slim's door is always open.

intro.text: Certificates in a nylon bag, CV printed at a business centre, and one good shirt. Walk the city, find work, build something. Open your phone for jobs, loans, contacts and the map.
